title: An Important and Solemn Communiqué from Me
author: Greg Ashman
summary: Ashman critiques the Australian Association for Research in Education (AARE) for losing relevance to teachers and policymakers, then attempting gatekeeping rather than reform. The AARE's communiqué redefines 'evidence' broadly to include fashionable but unrigorous approaches, dismisses work by thinktanks as lacking 'safeguards,' and pushes antiracism as unquestionable precept rather than open intellectual question. The association's real problem is its own irrelevance: grassroots movements like researchED now fill the void by actually serving teachers. Gatekeeping and redefinition of 'evidence' represent performative virtue signaling rather than commitment to rigor or relevance.
points: ResearchED drew 700 educators on Saturday because teachers value practical evidence; AARE loses relevance by writing primarily for other academics.
AARE's redefinition of 'evidence' opens the door to unrigorous work while appearing inclusive.
The gatekeeping effort admits AARE's own irrelevance: their main problem is not media coverage but lack of relevance entirely.
Calls to 'embed antiracism' insert a precept beyond argument, contradicting academic freedom researchers claim to value.
Education academics have abandoned free inquiry for performative virtue—calling for fashionable ideas to look good before peers.
quotes: They still have nothing useful to say, but they want to be the ones to say it.

The AARE couldn't care less about being useful to teachers or policymakers. It's all just a performance.” “Imagine if medical researchers said: well, whether homeopathy is effective constitutes a positivistic and harmful reductive binary.” Archived from Filling the Pail on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
